response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view, 2026-11-21
CLINICAL INDICATION: Emergency department. Shortness of breath. History of prostate cancer on hormone therapy. Portable film.
ORDERING PROVIDER: Dr. J. Marte, ED
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph, 2026-06-30
TECHNIQUE: Current film is AP, labeled supine and portable, with low inspiration and mild rotation. Prior film is PA with adequate inspiration and mild rotation. Projection differs from the prior. Position, inspiration and exposure also differ. Comparison is limited.

LOOK AT FIRST:
- F1 (devices): Tubular density over the tracheal air column, consistent with an endotracheal tube, tip over the upper thoracic trachea. Carina not clearly seen. Not present on the prior. Status is indeterminate because the two blind reads disagreed (read A: new; read B: stable). Tip-to-carina relationship to be confirmed on the source image.
- F3 (right mid zone): Increased coarse reticular and hazy perihilar opacity compared with the prior. Both reads agreed. Supine AP technique contributes in part.
- F4 (left mid zone): Increased coarse reticular and hazy perihilar opacity compared with the prior. Both reads agreed. Supine AP technique contributes in part.
- F5 (right lower zone): Hazy opacity with indistinct right hemidiaphragm margin. Indeterminate (both reads indeterminate). Atelectasis, airspace opacity and layering pleural fluid are all possible.
- F6 (left lower zone): Hazy opacity at the left base and retrocardiac region with poorly defined left hemidiaphragm. Indeterminate (both reads indeterminate). Atelectasis, airspace opacity and layering pleural fluid are all possible.

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Trachea roughly midline allowing for rotation. Tubular density over the tracheal air column as described in F1. Lung volumes are low. Bilateral coarse reticular and hazy opacities in the perihilar, mid and lower zones (F3, F4), with denser hazy opacity at the right base (F5) and the left base and retrocardiac region (F6). No focal mass is seen within the limits of the film. Prior: well inflated lungs, mild prominence of right perihilar and lower zone markings, no confluent consolidation, no discrete nodule or mass.
- Mediastinum / hila: Upper mediastinum looks broad on this AP supine film, so width is not reliable (F8: indeterminate, not comparable; only one read recorded it). Hila are indistinct with perihilar haze, more evident on the right. Prior: mediastinal contour not widened for a PA film, hila mildly prominent on the right with rotation contributing, no discrete hilar mass.
- Pleura: No pleural line is seen, but a supine film is insensitive for pneumothorax. Hazy increased density over both lower zones with indistinct costophrenic regions; layering effusions cannot be excluded. Prior: no pneumothorax, no large effusion, left costophrenic angle partly obscured by the enlarged heart.
- Heart: Cardiac silhouette enlarged, but AP supine projection and low volumes magnify it. Left heart border partly indistinct. Prior also showed an enlarged silhouette on a PA film. Interval size change cannot be judged (F7: indeterminate, not comparable; both reads indeterminate).
- Bones / soft tissue: No displaced rib or clavicle fracture, though fine bone detail is limited on the portable film. No soft tissue gas. Both domes are high, consistent with low inspiration and supine position; no free gas seen, though a supine film is insensitive. Devices: Left pectoral cardiac device with multiple transvenous leads, including shock coils over the superior vena cava and right ventricle regions, with no lead discontinuity seen at this resolution. F2 status is indeterminate because the reads disagreed (read A: stable; read B: new). The same lead configuration is present on both films; the right ventricular coil projects lower on the current film, which is expected from the change in projection, position and inspiration. ECG electrodes and external lines overlie the chest. A looped density over the lower midline may be an enteric tube or external hardware.

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: Increased coarse reticular and hazy perihilar opacity in the right mid zone (F3) and left mid zone (F4), both reads agreed. Right base (F5) and left base (F6) are denser or less well defined than on the prior, but are indeterminate because of technique. Tubular density over the trachea is not seen on the prior; its status is indeterminate and the reads disagreed (F1, read A: new; read B: stable). Size change in words: not applicable for these findings.
- Unchanged: Left pectoral cardiac device and lead configuration are present on both films, but the device status is indeterminate and the reads disagreed (F2, read A: stable; read B: new). Cardiac silhouette is enlarged on both films, but change in size cannot be judged (F7). Upper mediastinal width cannot be compared (F8).

RECIST 1.1: Not computed. No confirmed measurements.

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Has the heart size changed? | Reason: Prior is PA and current is AP supine portable with low inspiration. Magnification differs between the two. | Recommend: Repeat PA and lateral when the patient is able, or echocardiography or CT chest if clinically needed.
- Are pleural effusions present, and are they new? (read A) | Reason: On a supine film fluid layers posteriorly and appears as hazy density rather than a meniscus. Both bases are hazy, with low volumes also contributing. | Recommend: Upright or decubitus film, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest.
- Is there a left pleural effusion or left lower zone collapse behind the heart? (read A) | Reason: Retrocardiac density on a single frontal supine film, with an enlarged heart and a poorly defined left hemidiaphragm. | Recommend: Lateral view when the patient is able, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest.
- Is the basal opacity true consolidation or atelectasis from low volumes? (read A) | Reason: Current film is supine with low lung volumes, which crowds the lower zones and mimics basal opacity. | Recommend: Repeat film with better inspiration when possible, or CT chest.
- Is the endotracheal tube tip at a satisfactory level above the carina, and is an enteric tube present? (read A) | Reason: The carina is not clearly defined on this compressed image. Multiple external lines and a looped density over the lower midline overlap the mediastinum and upper abdomen. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS with windowing. Repeat the film after removing external lines from the field if position remains unclear.
- Have the cardiac device lead tips moved? (read A) | Reason: Different projection, position and inspiration change the projected position of the leads over the heart. | Recommend: Review in PACS against the prior. If displacement is a clinical concern, obtain PA and lateral films when the patient is able and a device check.
- Is there a small pneumothorax? (reads A and B) | Reason: A supine film is insensitive, because air collects anteriorly and at the bases. No pleural line is seen, but that does not exclude it. | Recommend: Upright or decubitus film, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest if clinically suspected.
- Is the upper mediastinum truly wider than before? (read A) | Reason: AP supine projection and rotation widen the mediastinal shadow compared with the PA upright prior. | Recommend: Repeat upright PA when the patient is able, or CT chest if clinically indicated.
- Are there small lung nodules on either study? (read A) | Reason: The portable film has low contrast and diffuse opacities. The device generator and external hardware obscure parts of both lungs. Small nodules are not reliably seen on X-ray. | Recommend: CT chest if clinically relevant.
- Are there pleural effusions, and are they new? (read B) | Reason: On a supine film fluid layers posteriorly and shows only as a hazy veil. The lower zones are also crowded by low volumes. | Recommend: Upright or decubitus film, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest.
- Is there a left pleural effusion or retrocardiac collapse or consolidation? (read B) | Reason: The left base is hidden behind the heart on a low-volume supine AP film. The left costophrenic angle was already slightly hazy on the prior. | Recommend: Upright PA and lateral when the patient is able, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest.
- Is the basal opacity true new airspace disease or an effect of technique? (read B) | Reason: Low inspiration and supine position crowd the lower zones and mimic basal opacity. | Recommend: Repeat film with better inspiration, upright if possible, or CT chest.
- Is an endotracheal tube present, and where is its tip relative to the carina? Is an enteric tube present, and where does it end? (read B) | Reason: The tube outline and carina are not clearly resolved on this compressed image, and overlying leads and wires confuse the midline. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS with windowing and confirm tube positions clinically. Repeat the film if the tip is not seen.
- Is the mediastinum widened? (read B) | Reason: Supine AP projection with mild rotation and low volumes widens the mediastinal shadow. | Recommend: Repeat upright PA when the patient is able, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.

IMPRESSION:
1. Tubular density over the trachea, consistent with an endotracheal tube, not seen on the prior (F1). Indeterminate: the two reads disagreed (read A: new; read B: stable). Tip is over the upper thoracic trachea and the carina is not clearly seen, so position is undetermined.
2. Increased coarse reticular and hazy perihilar opacity in the right and left mid zones compared with the prior (F3, F4), both reads agreed. Pattern is consistent with interstitial fluid or another diffuse process. Supine AP technique contributes in part.
3. Hazy opacity at the right base and at the left base and retrocardiac region (F5, F6), indeterminate. Atelectasis, airspace opacity and layering pleural fluid are all possible. Low volumes and supine position can mimic this.
4. Left pectoral cardiac device with transvenous leads present on both films (F2). Lead position status is indeterminate and the reads disagreed (read A: stable; read B: new). No lead discontinuity seen at this resolution.
5. Enlarged cardiac silhouette on both films and apparent upper mediastinal broadening (F7, F8) are not comparable between PA upright and AP supine films. Pleural effusion, pneumothorax and small nodules cannot be determined. No discrete lung mass or definite focal bone lesion is seen at this resolution.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- Review the source image in PACS with windowing now to confirm endotracheal tube tip relative to the carina, any enteric tube, and device lead position against the prior.
- Repeat the chest film after removing external lines from the field if tube position remains unclear.
- Repeat upright PA and lateral chest radiograph when the patient is able, with better inspiration.
- Upright or decubitus film, bedside ultrasound, or CT chest if effusion, pneumothorax or nodules are clinically suspected.
- Device check and PA and lateral films when the patient is able if lead displacement is a clinical concern.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
